clue.text: Head appearing stoned in India, back in the day?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a crown (head) with a gem set in it
second meaning: India was called the finest possession of the British Empire

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoned' looks like drugged, but it means set with stones; the phrase also names India's place in the old British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was used of colonial India as the most prized part of the British Empire, and literally describes a gem set in a royal headpiece.

clue.text: Proper wages for unhelpful official

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: what a job is worth
second meaning: a petty official who sticks to the rules to avoid helping

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer is literally the worth of a job; as one word it is British slang for an obstructive jobsworth clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a minor functionary who refuses help, saying it's more than his post is worth to bend the rules.

clue.text: Mounting a stage that is wide, making a bloomer

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the letters climb upwards, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: An actor climbing onto a broad stage makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Weigela is a flowering garden shrub, and a bloomer is anything that flowers.

clue.text: Length of wait spelled out in detail, maybe to extremes

indicators.note: spelled out suggests the letters of detail are laid out afresh in another order
to extremes means only the outermost letters of maybe are used

parts.note: outer letters M and E

explanation.surface: Someone explains in detail how long the wait will be, perhaps exaggerating.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead time is the interval between ordering something and its delivery, a period one waits.

clue.text: Elbow say brownish, seen from underneath

indicators.note: in a down clue, viewing from below means reading the letters upward

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is signalled by 'say'
dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A description of a brownish elbow viewed from below.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to give them a push or prod with the arm.

clue.text: Serious consequences as that fellow will always secure first place

indicators.note: secure means hold firmly, so the outer pieces grip the inner one between them

parts.note: he'll is the contraction for 'he will'
ay (aye) is an old word for always
top is the first or highest position

explanation.surface: A warning that a man determined to always win will pay dearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell to pay is an idiom for severe trouble or punishment to come.

clue.text: No hero takes care of a room full of the sick

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of

parts.words: a room full of the sick
parts.note: a ward is a hospital room for patients

explanation.surface: An unheroic person looks after a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward lacks courage, the opposite of a brave hero.

clue.text: More than time one was put on to bowl?

definitions.text: More than time one was put on to bowl?

parts.words: More than time one was put on to bowl?
parts.note: in cricket a bowler sends down a set of six balls; a bowler kept waiting is owed that set

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer describes a cricket bowler waiting for his turn of six balls; as one word it means late.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue is late, past the time it was expected.

clue.text: Viking raid — no help is secured by hooter

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: hooter is slang for a nose

indicators.note: no help means the letters of 'help' are taken out

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A Viking raid goes unaided and is caught by a siren.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings were Scandinavians, and Norse describes their people and language.

clue.text: Robber gang seizing equipment

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a band is a gang
rig means equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: A criminal gang steals some equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, one of a gang who rob travellers.

clue.text: Change down into this mean outfit

parts.note: low means mean or base
gear means clothes, an outfit

explanation.surface: Someone advised to change into a shabby outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like changing clothes, but it is a driver shifting down a gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver shifting to a slower ratio of the gearbox moves into a lower setting.

clue.text: In grief stop listening

indicators.note: listening says we take the word as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: whoa is a command to stop, given to a horse

explanation.surface: A grieving person cuts off from hearing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is deep sorrow or distress.

clue.text: Better grind out time in the middle here?

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Advice to a batsman to grind out a long innings at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: Trent Bridge is a Test cricket ground in Nottingham; 'time in the middle' is batting time at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Batsmen spend their innings in the middle of this Nottingham cricket ground, a Test venue.

clue.text: Believe me, if you have a hearing impairment …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a phrase insisting you take my word

definitions.text: if you have a hearing impairment
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what a deaf listener might be asked to do, lipread

explanation.walkthrough: The catchphrase is famous from George H. W. Bush's 1988 tax pledge; literally it invites a deaf person to follow speech by sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic pledge to be trusted, and literally asks someone to watch the mouth to follow speech.

clue.text: Owns article one sort of dog ate, so getting another dog

indicators.note: ate means swallowed up, so the dog holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a lap dog is a sort of dog
has means owns
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dog wolfs down someone's property, which brings in a second dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lhasa apso is a small long-haired Tibetan breed of canine.

clue.text: One bound to be partial to browser (Firefox)

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are fond of the Firefox web browser.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a feudal labourer tied to the land, so bound in servitude.

clue.text: Definite final word: leader in television is Sky

parts.note: firm means definite, settled
amen is the last word of a prayer

indicators.note: leader in means the first letter of television

explanation.surface: A definite final verdict: the top person in TV is Sky, the broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' looks like the British satellite TV company, but it is the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the heavens overhead.

clue.text: Protein in body once developed to limit rising bile

indicators.note: to limit means to bound on both sides, so these letters hold the others
developed means changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: gall is bile

explanation.surface: A physiology note on a protein that once evolved to restrict bile.
explanation.definitionFit: Collagen is the main structural protein of skin, tendons and connective tissue.

clue.text: African is talking to whom?

indicators.note: talking says the words are heard spoken aloud

parts.note: said casually, 'to whom?' becomes 'who to?'

explanation.surface: Someone asks who an African is talking to.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are the majority ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Ultimately smart suit needed for creative activities

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of smart

parts.note: hearts is one of the four suits of playing cards

explanation.surface: A smart suit is ultimately what creative people need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing, but it is a suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The arts are painting, music, literature and other creative pursuits.

clue.text: Young Australian? He must be about 70!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a boomer is a large male kangaroo
second meaning: someone born in the post-war birth boom, about seventy when this was set

explanation.walkthrough: 'Young Australian' suggests a person, but a boomer is a male kangaroo; the other sense is the post-war generation.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names people born in the birth surge after 1945, and jokingly a young kangaroo.

clue.text: In bombing raid perhaps, fail to wipe out southern end of Scottish island

parts.note: to miss is to fail

indicators.text: to wipe out southern end of
indicators.note: in a down clue the southern end is the bottom, the last letter, which is removed

parts.note: Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: In an air raid a bomber fails to destroy the south of a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is an operational flight, such as a single sortie by a bomber.

clue.text: Raised mark on skin round dry blotchy area

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a mole is a raised dark spot on the skin
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A dermatologist's note: a raised mark beside a dry, blotchy patch of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A mottle is a spot or patch of blotchy colour, as on mottled skin.

clue.text: Old reptile's power badly tore foot

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: badly means messed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: a dactyl is a metrical foot, long then two short syllables

explanation.surface: A prehistoric beast's strength badly tore someone's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' looks anatomical, but it is a unit of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The pterodactyl was a flying reptile of the Jurassic period, long extinct.

clue.text: Contemptuous expression puts playwright under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, the playwright sits beneath the other letter, so it comes second

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Someone scornful puts a dramatist under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an exclamation of disdain or impatience.

clue.text: Cast finished speaking

indicators.note: speaking says the words are taken as heard aloud

parts.note: through means finished, done

explanation.surface: A theatre cast has finished its lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a theatre company, but it is the past tense of throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast and threw are both past tenses of verbs meaning to fling.

clue.text: Black for one short layer of coal

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a seam is a layer of coal underground

explanation.surface: Black, as an example, lacks a thin stratum of coal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' looks like the colour of coal, but it is the Black Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea is an example of an inland body of salt water.

clue.text: Parking not easy to get in van or car

parts.note: hard means not easy
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A grumble that it is awkward to park and climb into a van or car.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a motor vehicle with a rigid roof, as opposed to a soft-topped convertible.

clue.text: Scrap broadcast about jazz

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to emit is to send out, broadcast

explanation.surface: A radio programme about jazz gets scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is an early syncopated piano style that fed into jazz.

clue.text: Saying pale child, name concealed, is perhaps now 11 books ahead

indicators.note: ahead means placed in front, so these letters come before the rest

parts.note: someone who is now eleven was ten a year ago
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
wan means pale

indicators.note: concealed means hidden inside, so the letter goes within the child

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A tale of a pale child whose name is hidden, now aged eleven and well ahead in reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is 'is perhaps now 11': a child who is eleven now was ten before, so WAS TEN. That and OT go ahead of the pale child.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a proverb urging thrift: if you avoid squandering, you will never go short.
